caseno: Appeal From Appellate Decree No. 685 of 1970
lawyer: Mr. M. Nurullah, advocate ----- for the appellants.
parties:
Abdul Khaleque and ors. ----- Appellants
Vs
Abdul Khalek and ors. ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
This appeal is by the plaintiffs who have lost in both the courts. They claimed tenancy right under Bhawal Court of Wards Estate. They set out their case with the premises that the predecessors of the plaintiffs were given barga settlement, as there was prohibition by the order of the Board of Revenue to grant long term settlement of the land to the tenants under the Court of Wards. They, however, set up the case that subsequently they were granted the status of tenants and recognised as such. In support of their claim the plaintiffs mainly relied on two sets of rent receipts. One is Exhibits 1 (series) which describes them as bargadars, and the other Exhibit G series which describes them as `proja'. They also filed certain Kabalas, gifts, mortgage created by them to show that they were recognised as tenants by the Court of Wards. The trial court negatived all the contentions and dismissed the suit. On appeal the court of appeal below has found that the plaintiffs claimed tenancy right under the court of wards which was controlled by the Board of Revenue and there was express prohibition of grant of long term settlements Exhibit 1 series described them as Bargadars. No doubt, Exhibit G series describes them as 'projas'. Exhibit G series was considered by the court of appeal below and the found that the expression of proja will not change the character of a bargadar, if he is not a tenant. He came to the basic question that the plaintiffs have totally failed to establish that they get any settlement upon proper sanction from the court of wards of their tenancies. He also found that there is no evidence that the subsequent acts of these plaintiffs by kabala, mortgage or gifts were ever consented to be the landlord, namely, the court of wards. He also found that though in the rent receipts they rents were realised in specie, still they stand as equivalent to the barta crops and that is why the were raised from time to time. The court appeal below further held that the plaintiffs witnesses are also not uniform as to the persons possessing the lands, the evidence of some of the P.Ws. being 45 persons are in possession, whereas 92 persons have claimed tenancy right as plaintiffs. He found that the P.Ws. are also not uniform in their evidence as to the length of possession. He, therefore, dismissed the appeal. 

 2. It is to be noted that another appeal being Title Appeal No. 134 of 1964 was heard from another suit along with the present and where the defendants 1 and 2 were parties, and that appeal has been disposed of by this court on 15.2.62 and it does not concern us. We are concerned with the suit filed by the plaintiffs and the appeal therefore which is Title Appeal No. 157 of 1964. 

 3. Mr. M. Nurullah submits that there are two series of rent receipts on record, one Exhibit 1 series showing the plaintiffs as bargadars, and the other Exhibit G series showing them as projas. He further submits that the rents were realised in specie which go to show that the plaintiffs were tenants and the courts below have misconceived these rent receipts. We fail to see how these are questions of law. The words 'Bargadar' and 'Projas' have been written in Bengali and they have been considered as it should be considered by the court. We should not forget the plaintiffs' basic case is that their predecessors took the land as bargadars and so they carried a heavy onus on them to show that at any time subsequent to the creation of the barga rights they were ever converted into permanent tenancies and they were recognised as such. They have failed to discharge this onus as found by the court of appeal below, there being no evidence to sustain them. We are to remember that the landlord, the court of wards was governed by its own rules and procedure, and it is not disputed that the Rule was that without the sanction of the Board of Revenue no long term settlement could be given and that is totally lacking in this case.
